purpose: P3-S8 A-07: the runtime grant matrix over the DISCOVERED Phase 3 surface — every relation a database built from 0000 through phase2PrefixEnd does not have, which is Phase 3 and every phase after it. For every runtime principal and PUBLIC: the exact SELECT on each such table (table or column level), no write privilege of any kind, and the exact routines it may EXECUTE.
source: infrastructure/database/migrations/0053_inventory_units_and_product_configuration.sql through 0073_default_warehouse_locale_name.sql (the Phase 3 corrective 0070-0073 included) for the Phase 3 scope; 0074_phase4_registry_widening.sql onwards for the entries beyond it.
note: This file is the INTENDED model. The P3-S8 grant-matrix suite (T-04) compares it against the live PostgreSQL catalogues, in both directions: an entry here that the database does not grant is a broken deployment, and a grant the database holds that is absent here is an unreviewed privilege. That comparison runs over the WHOLE discovered surface, Phase 4's own relations included, because it is a law over whatever exists rather than a claim about what will: a migration that grants SELECT on a new table is red until a reviewer records the grant here, which is exactly the change a reviewer must see. Editing this file does not widen anything; a migration does. The one entry that is an INVENTORY rather than a law is phase3Tables, and it is the inventory of the PHASE 3 SCOPE alone — the relations the accepted, digest-verified files 0053 through phase3ScopeEnd create (P4-AL-88): 0000-0073 is frozen byte for byte, so no later phase can enter that scope, and 'and nothing more' still holds of it. A relation a later phase creates is outside that inventory and inside every law.

excludedFromRuntime.daftar_migrator: the deployment principal, not a runtime credential

forbiddenPrivilegesApplyTo: every runtime principal and PUBLIC, on every Phase 3 table, at table and at column level

executeNotes.daftar_app: The 27 signed entry routines (one per registered operation kind) plus the two INVOKER read functions purchase_ap_outstanding and purchase_settlement_state (0065, replaced in 0067 and, purchase_ap_outstanding, in 0072). S7 adds none; S8 adds none; the Phase 3 corrective 0072 (TD-16) adds purchase_write_off_residue, the routine of its one operation kind. Beyond the Phase 3 scope, 0078 adds sale_commit, the signed entry routine of the sale.commit operation kind, granted to daftar_app and to nobody else — its three helpers (sale_lock_commit_targets, sale_document_number, sale_bridge_commit) carry no EXECUTE grant at all, so the only way into them is the entry routine's own DEFINER body. And 0075 adds the four INVOKER receivables read functions — invoice_outstanding, invoice_settlement_state, customer_ar_outstanding and customer_ar_aging — granted to daftar_app and to daftar_inventory_internal, and to nobody else; PUBLIC holds EXECUTE on none of them. And 0081 adds the two signed entry routines of P4-S4 — customer_collect_payment (the customer.collect_payment kind) and customer_apply_credit (the customer.apply_credit kind) — each a DEFINER routine owned by daftar_inventory_internal, EXECUTE REVOKEd from PUBLIC and granted to daftar_app and to nobody else (0081:2439-2442). Their helpers carry no EXECUTE grantee at all — the three deferred verification helpers invoice_settlement_verify, payment_closure_verify and customer_credit_verify, the seven guard and value-completion triggers, and the one writer customer_credit_consume (0081:1253-1263, 1716-1718) — so the only way into any of them is an entry routine's own DEFINER body or the deferred constraint trigger that PERFORMs it. 0081 also REPLACEs the body of invoice_outstanding(uuid,uuid), whose 0075 grant to daftar_app and daftar_inventory_internal is unchanged and already recorded above.
executeNotes.daftar_platform: The two inventory key-domain routines (L:1868) plus the three provisioning routines 0070 (TD-18) re-created and handed to daftar_provisioning_internal: provision_actor(text[]) and the provisioning key install/retire commands. Each keeps its accepted Phase 1 grant to the platform alone; TD-18 closed the TL-3 exception set (no replaced routine is owned by the applier or pins a public-first path any more).
executeNotes.public: No Phase 3 routine, definer or invoker, is executable by PUBLIC.
executeNotes.beyondPhase3Scope: Entries for relations and routines a later phase creates are reviewed here on the same terms as the Phase 3 ones. They are NOT an allowlist that admits them: they are the reviewed statement of which grants exist, and every law in the suite — the forbidden privileges, the by-USE DML refusal sweep, the definer law — still applies to them in full.

internalWriterTablePrivilegesBeyondPhase.note: NOT a law of this file and NOT an allowlist: the laws above are about the seven runtimePrincipals and PUBLIC, and daftar_inventory_internal is neither — it is the DEFINER-owner the signed entry routines run as, so a table privilege it holds is reachable only from inside a routine it owns. This entry exists because a reviewer should not have to read a migration to learn that an internal writer gained a WRITE privilege, which is the one thing the grant matrix cannot report. It records the Phase 4 ones and what withholds the rest.

pos_till_sessions: UPDATE (status, closed_at, close_intent_sha256, closing_count_minor, business_transaction_id) only

internalWriterTablePrivilegesBeyondPhase.whyInvoiceSequencesTakesBoth: TL-P4-S2-R4. INSERT is the FIRST-USE INITIALISER: 0078's sale_commit creates the (business_id, 'invoice', YYYY) series row of a business that has never numbered a document, with the default internal format INV-{YYYY}-{SEQ:6}, as INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (business_id, document_kind, period) DO NOTHING. Before the ruling the routine REFUSED instead, which left a clean business with no supported path to its first invoice number. The UPDATE is COLUMN-LEVEL on updated_at alone and is the ROW LOCK's: every PostgreSQL locking clause requires UPDATE on the relation, satisfied by any one column (0045:399 is the precedent). The two together are deliberately not enough to rewrite a merchant's number_format: INSERT can only create, DO NOTHING never overwrites, there is no table-level UPDATE and no UPDATE on number_format, so ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is not even a privilege the owner holds. 0078-E(5) asserts the body carries exactly one INSERT, that it is DO NOTHING, and that it UPDATEs and DELETEs the relation nowhere; 0078-E(7) asserts the privileges against the live catalogues, including that NO runtime principal holds INSERT on the series. Proved behaviourally in tests/integration/sale-s2-sequence-init.test.ts. This is a DAFTAR-INTERNAL document identifier and implies no jurisdiction's fiscal or tax rule: OD-03 is OPEN (P4-AL-45).
internalWriterTablePrivilegesBeyondPhase.whyThePosRelationsTakeThose: P4-S3, 0079 section 4. daftar_app holds SELECT and EXECUTE and NO DML on either relation (P4-AL-38), so the four pos_* commands are the only writers and they run as this internal DEFINER owner. Every UPDATE is COLUMN-LEVEL and never table-level: on the session exactly the five closing columns, so neither `opened_by` nor `opening_float_minor` is writable — OD-P4-09 is a privilege-level fact as well as a constraint, and a counted opening float that could be rewritten after the shift opened would not be a counted float (R-P4-S3-09); on a cart line exactly the quantity, the DISCOUNT REQUEST and the removal TOMBSTONE, so a line's product and its actor are not revisable. There is no DELETE and no TRUNCATE on either relation, for anyone: the accepted estate's append-only clause (tests/security/inventory-db-authority.test.ts:284-291) gives this principal no DELETE on a relation beyond the accepted prefix, and the first full-estate round of P4-S3 refused an earlier draft that granted one. So a basket is the append-only record of its shift, removing a line writes removed_at, the line ordinal is held by a PARTIAL unique index WHERE removed_at IS NULL so the till may reuse it, and pos_cart_line_guard() refuses a DELETE outright. 0079-E(6) asserts both writable column sets and that nobody but the owner holds DELETE or TRUNCATE on either relation. There is deliberately NO DELETE on pos_till_sessions — a shift is history the moment it opens — and there IS one on pos_cart_lines, because removing a line from a basket is what a till does; pos_cart_line_guard() binds every write, the removal included, to an OPEN session, so a closed shift's basket is frozen evidence. 0079-E(6) asserts all of it against the live catalogues, including that no runtime principal holds DML or any column privilege and that the internal writer holds no table-level UPDATE behind the column grants. P4-S3 creates NO accounting object, so daftar_accounting_internal holds nothing on either relation (0079-E(2), 0079-E(5)).
internalWriterTablePrivilegesBeyondPhase.whyTheReceivablesSettlementRelationsTake: P4-S4, 0081 section 2 (0081:615-618, 660-661). daftar_app holds SELECT and EXECUTE and NO DML on any of the four relations (P4-AL-38), so customer_collect_payment and customer_apply_credit are the only writers and they run as this internal DEFINER owner. INSERT ONLY on payments, payment_allocations and customer_credit_applications: a payment, an allocation and a credit application are history the moment they are recorded, there is no table-level UPDATE, no DELETE and no TRUNCATE on any of them for anyone, and the deferred value-completion triggers (0081:972, 1006, 1141) judge the inserted row rather than trusting the wrapper that computed it. customer_credits takes INSERT plus a COLUMN-LEVEL UPDATE on exactly remaining_amount_minor and remaining_carrying_base_amount_minor (0081:617), the pair R-90’s one writer customer_credit_consume (0081:1224) decrements together; no other column of a credit — not its original amount, not its currency, not its rate — is writable, so a credit’s face value cannot be rewritten after it is issued. The two GRANT UPDATE (status) on invoices and customers (0081:660-661) are the ROW-LOCK ACL and nothing else: PostgreSQL requires SELECT plus one of UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE for a locking clause and honours it on the strength of UPDATE on any single column, so this is the narrowest list the five FOR UPDATE / FOR SHARE locks of 0081:1987, 2014, 2024, 2299 and 2345 accept (0045:399 is the precedent, and 0081:617 already covers the customer_credits lock while 0067:648-650 already covers payment_methods). NEITHER routine issues any UPDATE on invoices or customers — every UPDATE token in either body is the word inside a FOR UPDATE clause — and tests/guards/p4s4-settlement-surface-laws.test.ts holds that permanently. Behind the status column each table still has a guard this role cannot lift: invoices_lifecycle_guard() (0075:546) and customers_revision_guard() (0075:516), whose FUNCTIONS this role owns but whose TABLES stay with the migrator (0075:642-647), so ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER is refused. daftar_accounting_internal gains SELECT on all four and no write of any kind (0081:618): a validator that cannot read its source row passes vacuously, and it posts through the journal objects it already owns.

prePhase3TableRuntimePrivileges.note: The table-level runtime privileges on the pre-Phase-3 tables that gained a Phase 3 column: exactly the frozen Phase 1 set (0006:77-78, the defect of L:9), identical at 0052 and at 0069. Every Phase 3 column on them is protected by its named invoker guard.
